newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia mines ministry to check Busang reports.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia mines ministry to check Busang reports.

text.p: Indonesian Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Sunday his department would check newspaper reports that Bre-X Minerals Ltd had manipulated data on its Busang gold deposit in Kalimantan.

"Frankly speaking, I only knew about it after I read it in the papers. But if it is indeed true, like it or not, Indonesia will lose because they have already deceived people," Sudjana was quoted as saying by the official Antara news agency.

Citing unnamed sources, Indonesia's Harian Ekonomi Neraca newspaper on Friday reported that a review by Busang partner Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc showed the deposit was smaller than Bre-X's estimate of 71 million ounces.
"It is possible that the deposit is not as big as has been mentioned before. It could be that it is not viable to mine this deposit," the newspaper said, quoting the source.
New Orleans-based Freeport said on Friday its review of the site was not finished. A spokeswoman for the local Indonesian partners said this could take up to four weeks more.
Sudjana said the report still had to be proved true.
"Because of that, just wait until later this week when we have done the checks. I promise if this report is indeed true, there will be action from the government," he said.
Trading in shares in the Calgary, Alberta-based prospector was temporarily halted on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Friday after the report hit the market.
The uncertainty was amplified by the death of Bre-X chief geologist Michael de Guzman, a co-discoverer of the Busang gold deposit.
De Guzman, who fell out of a helicopter on Wednesday while flying to the gold site in Indonesia's East Kalamantan province, was ill and may have committed suicide, Indonesian officials said.
Antara on Sunday quoted rescue officials as saying De Guzman's body had not been found.
